intro.title: useDeferredValue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple search input that filters a large list of items. You will learn how to use the React hook `useDeferredValue` to improve performance by deferring a state update, preventing the UI from freezing during expensive filtering operations. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the `useDeferredValue` hook. This concept helps keep your application responsive by allowing urgent updates (like typing) to happen immediately while non-urgent updates (like filtering results) can be delayed. By the end, you'll understand how to apply `useDeferredValue` to manage slow, non-blocking state transitions in a user-friendly way.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useDeferredValue shines in search interfaces where users type queries and expect immediate visual feedback while heavy filtering happens in the background. Think of e-commerce sites like Amazon or streaming services like Netflix—as you type in the search bar, the UI remains responsive showing placeholder results or loading states, while the actual product or movie filtering defers to prevent jank. This pattern is also crucial in data dashboards with complex visualizations, where user interactions with filters don't block UI updates. By deferring non-critical updates, developers ensure typing feels instantaneous while computationally expensive operations like filtering large datasets don't freeze the interface.
